title: Comprehensive study of three years of AI games on Steam
author: perelmanych
selftext: Sulka Haro in his data driven [study](https://fragwyz.substack.com/p/three-years-of-ai-on-steam) of 3 years of AI games on Steam has a good news and a bad news for you.

comments.author: witmann_pl
comments.body: What I'm getting from this analysis is that AI pushback exists, but is smaller than what Reddit and other information bubbles make it look like. Not surprising, TBH. If you put effort into making a good game, it will be viewed as a good game, however expect some negative reviews because "AI slop".

replies.author: theflossboss1
replies.body: What I’m getting is that there are so many games coming out now with AI… just no one seems to be buying them

replies.author: witmann_pl
replies.body: No one is buying most of the games coming out regardless if they used AI or not.

replies.author: perelmanych
replies.body: Yes, that is sad reality we are living in. Winner takes it all.

replies.author: N1ghtshade3
replies.body: It's not sad. There's no barrier to entry for putting something on Steam. Every time some nobody throws their crappy beginner project onto the store, the percentage of games that succeed goes down. It means nothing.

replies.author: perelmanych
replies.body: The problem is not that there is fat tail of failed projects which deserve that. The problem is that there is virtually no room for middle class games. I mean there are a lot of such games but the share of money they all compete is negligible, at most like 5% of all money.

replies.author: god-damn-the-usa
replies.body: most games are lazy and ugly

comments.author: DerrickBarra
comments.body: That's very interesting. So 1/3 games released in 2026 use some form of AI, and if the predicted rise in adoption continues, it will be around 60% by 2028. That's not unexpected. As the tooling only got 'good' for most engineers around winter of 2025. And we've seen a lot of agentic tooling and workflows experimented since then. I would expect the adoption to keep increasing until it hits a natural plateau (you'll never get 100% adoption of any tool, but it will be the majority as it makes sense to use the tool for each dev or touches the production in some way).

replies.author: SavingsChicken1572
replies.body: tbh I dont think any game after 2026 is completely free from AI. if someone asks chatgpt about even history or w/e for lore in their game, they are using AI. let alone the coding or research.

replies.author: DerrickBarra
replies.body: pretty much, there's also the case that the underlying tools used were at least partially developed using AI post 2026.

replies.author: SavingsChicken1572
replies.body: I can even make a shell company that made everything AI, then sell everything to my other company labeling it as "not AI", then just act innocent with the other company.

comments.author: Accomplished-Fan9568
comments.body: Things are about to change friend.

replies.author: god-damn-the-usa
replies.body: yeah, soon the top 0.1% of games will capture 94% of revenue

replies.author: Accomplished-Fan9568
replies.body:
Well maybe maybe not, because in a near future typically noone will pay for games. Games will be like water from the tap, it already is.  
  
It would probably be more like 0.1% of games are paid for the rest are for free because there will simply be too many of them.

Anything AI can quickly generate will be worth absolutely nothing. Supply is infinite.

  
Gamers will likely make their own games and play a new one every evening, tailor made for their own taste..

comments.author: NotaDevAI
comments.body:
I thought hatred about using AI comes from not good quality. But joining reddit community made me realise there are indeed many people just hating it as soon as they know.

I'm really glad the actual research shows different vision than what I see in Reddit

replies.author: perelmanych
replies.body:
Any game could be slop it doesn't depend whether a game is AI free, AI assisted or fully vibe coded. 

Before I wrote two games by hand in C++ without any engine, only graphics library and they where so visually dull that I didn't publish them. TBS game was completely ready with like ten levels, units with special abilities and advanced AI that was calculating best move like in chess game, but visuals where meh at best. Now I can offload all the graphics side to AI, get good looking game and concentrate on the gameplay, models, story and level design.
